key_insight: Mach 4 flow over a microscale cylinder exhibits a wake transition from no clear unsteadiness to vortex shedding at St ≈ 0.2 and then dominance of a second mode at St ≈ 0.5, alongside independent bow-shock pulsations.
engineering_relevance: These instability regimes can inform unsteady-load and flow-control assessments for microscale bodies in supersonic, rarefied-to-near-continuum flows.
method: Direct Simulation Monte Carlo for a 30 μm cylinder at Mach 4 and Re = 270–6750.
Power spectral density analysis at discrete flow probes.
Dynamic mode decomposition of flowfield snapshots.
evidence_signal: Both analyses identify stagnation- and wake-region instabilities, with 10–15 MHz bow-shock pulsations present across all cases despite a 24-fold number-density variation.
watch_item: Bow-shock standoff distance is only a proposed control mechanism for pulsation, and the abstract does not establish broader applicability beyond the studied conditions.
paper_title: DSMC Study on Unsteadiness of Supersonic Flow Over a Cylinder
